name: DGN-410 / 460 / 520 Canister Filter
summary: A 24 V canister with a brushless DC pump, so you can wind the flow up or down instead of choking it with a tap. All three sizes share the same pump and footprint; the bigger numbers just add height and media space. The plain versions carry a 3 W UV lamp, the A versions leave it out.
highlights: Variable pump: 300 to 1,610 L/h at 4 to 30 W
Runs off an external 24 V adaptor
Same 24 x 24 cm footprint across all three sizes
3 W UV lamp on non-A models
bestFor: Mid to large planted tanks where you want to tune flow to the scape without swapping filters.
watchOut: The flow figure is shared across the range, so the larger bodies buy you media volume rather than extra flow.

specs.Variants: Standard (with 3 W UV) or A (no UV)

name: DGN-80 / 120 UVC Canister Filter
summary: A newer, white-bodied canister with a UVC lamp built in and a one-button prime. It comes in two sizes, each offered with or without the A suffix. Handy if green water has been a recurring headache, though a planted tank with good balance rarely needs UV running all the time.
highlights: Built-in UVC lamp with its own on/off switch
One-button air purge and siphon start
Clamp-lock lid and hidden carry handle
bestFor: Medium to large community tanks where the owner wants mechanical, biological and UV treatment in one box.
watchOut: Power draw is high for the flow (35 W and 55 W including the UV), and Boyu does not publish a recommended tank size.

name: WF Waterfall Hang-on Filter
summary: A simple hang-on-back filter that returns water as a wide waterfall, which keeps the surface moving and breaks up oily film. There are five sizes, from a tiny 150 L/h unit up to 720 L/h. Cheap and easy to service, but the splash does drive off CO2.
highlights: Layered media basket in the hang-on box
Surface skimming built in on the larger WF-2035 to 2055
bestFor: Small to medium low-tech tanks and shrimp or betta setups on a budget.
watchOut: The waterfall return gases off CO2, so it is not ideal on an injected tank, and Boyu gives no recommended tank sizes.

name: EF / EFU Canister Filter
summary: A no-frills external canister in six sizes, with shut-off valves built into the in and out ports so you can disconnect it for cleaning without draining hoses. The EFU versions are the same bodies with a 5 W UV lamp added. Flow ratings are modest, so treat the maker's tank ranges as generous.
highlights: Integrated shut-off valves on the head
EFU models add a 5 W UV lamp
bestFor: Budget-minded keepers with 100 to 650 litre tanks who want canister filtration and optional UV.
watchOut: The rated tank ranges are optimistic for a planted tank; size up if you want strong circulation.

specs.Valves: Built-in taps on inlet and outlet

name: FEF-230 / 280 Canister Filter
summary: A squarer canister with a built-in UV steriliser on its own switch and a valve block on the head for easy disconnection. Two sizes, each in two finishes. Flow is healthy for the power it uses.
highlights: Built-in UV with a separate switch
Valve block on the lid for quick disconnection
bestFor: Medium tanks around 150 to 300 litres where a budget UV canister makes sense.
watchOut: Boyu does not state the UV wattage or a recommended tank size.

name: SP-C / SP-B Internal Filter
summary: A submersible pump head sitting on one or two slotted sponge cartridges, which makes a simple internal filter that also aerates through a venturi. It is the classic cheap internal: effective at mechanical cleaning, easy to rinse, but bulky in a small scape.
highlights: Pump plus one or two sponge cylinders
Venturi air intake for extra oxygen
bestFor: Quarantine, hospital or grow-out tanks, and simple community tanks that need an easy internal filter.
watchOut: It is large and very visible in the tank, and the maker lists the SP-2300B with the same 8 W and 300 L/h as the small model, which looks like a sheet error.

name: SP-100 / SP-101 Series Powerhead
summary: A long-running range of small submersible powerheads with a venturi tube, a flow adjuster and an optional spray nozzle. Nine sizes run from a tiny 300 L/h unit to 1,850 L/h. Useful as a return pump, for driving an undergravel plate or just adding surface movement.
highlights: Venturi air injection and adjustable flow
bestFor: Anyone needing a cheap general-purpose pump for circulation, a DIY filter or a small sump return.
watchOut: The venturi and spray bar add a lot of surface agitation, which is not what you want on a CO2-injected tank.

name: SP-1000 Series Submersible Pump
summary: Compact multi-purpose submersible pumps that can push water, drive a fountain outlet or power a small filter. Five sizes from 300 to 1,400 L/h, with stainless steel shafts and resin-potted motors.
highlights: Up to 2 m head on the largest
Works as pump, fountain or filter pump
bestFor: Small sump returns, DIY filters and general water moving jobs around the fish room.
watchOut: Power use is on the high side for the flow on the bigger models (34 W for 1,400 L/h).

name: FP Series Submersible Pump
summary: Slim internal pumps supplied with a perforated spray bar, so they can filter, circulate or feed a fountain. Four sizes from 300 to 1,350 L/h, with permanent-magnet motors and stainless shafts.
highlights: Spray bar included for even flow along the tank
bestFor: Adding gentle, spread-out circulation to a medium tank or powering a simple internal filter.
watchOut: Spray bars sit high by design, so expect surface movement and some CO2 loss.

name: PGB Series Submersible Pump
summary: Tall, narrow submersible pumps with a long intake tube, built to sit upright in a corner or on an undergravel uplift. Three sizes from 740 to 1,565 L/h with up to 2.4 m of head.
bestFor: Undergravel plates, sump returns or DIY top filters that need decent head in a narrow space.

name: WM Series Wavemaker
summary: Round-bodied flow pumps that throw a broad, turbulent stream rather than a narrow jet, on a swivelling mount. The range covers single pumps (WM-101, WM-1, WM-2, WM-15), a 24 V magnet-mount WM-25, and multi-pump kits with a wave controller (WM-3 and WM-4).
highlights: Swivel mount points the flow any direction
WM-3 and WM-4 kits add a wave timer controller
WM-25 runs on DC 12 to 24 V, 5,500 L/h
bestFor: Medium and large planted tanks with dead spots behind hardscape, where you want circulation without a blasting jet.
watchOut: Boyu only gives flow for the WM-25; the others are rated by tank size, and the marketing leans towards marine use.

specs.Mounting: Suction cup / rim bracket, adjustable angle

name: WM-50 / WM-102 DC Wavemaker
summary: DC-driven wavemakers with an external digital controller that stores custom wave and flow programmes. WM-102 is a twin-pump set; WM-50 is a single, much stronger pump. Both run on a safe 24 V supply.
bestFor: Large tanks where you want adjustable, pulsed circulation from a controller.
watchOut: These are very strong pumps; most planted tanks will run them well below maximum.

name: HL Crossflow Wave Pump
summary: A tube-shaped crossflow pump that pushes a wide sheet of water along the tank, a bit like a gyre, and can also aerate. It uses a DC variable-speed drive with a digital display. Sizes run from a 20 cm unit to a 70 cm bar for very large aquariums.
highlights: DC variable speed with LED display
Can aerate as well as circulate
bestFor: Long tanks where you want even flow across the whole front-to-back depth.
watchOut: Boyu does not publish flow figures, and the two big models draw 100 to 200 W.

name: C Series Chiller
summary: Compact inline chillers for home aquariums, using R-134a refrigerant and a microprocessor thermostat. Three sizes cover roughly 50 to 600 litres. Worth a look if summer heat pushes your tank past what fans can handle.
highlights: Three sizes for about 50 to 600 L
bestFor: Planted tanks and shrimp tanks in hot climates that regularly creep above safe temperatures.
watchOut: Chillers dump heat into the room and need a pump or canister to push water through them.

name: LS Series Chiller
summary: A vertical chiller with a titanium heat exchanger and a digital temperature display. The plain models also include a heater, so one unit can hold temperature both ways; the A versions are cooling only.
highlights: Digital display and push-button set point
Non-A models add a 300 to 450 W heater
bestFor: Keepers who want year-round temperature control from one box on a medium to large tank.
watchOut: Rated flow through the unit is low (400 to 600 L/h), so check it matches your pump.

name: CW / LN Series Chiller
summary: Big box chillers for very large aquariums and fish rooms, rated from 500 up to 3,000 litres. Boyu lists the CW and LN codes with identical specs, and the LN range adds a 2 HP model.
bestFor: Very large display tanks or multi-tank systems in warm climates.
watchOut: They use R-22 refrigerant, which is phased out in many countries, so check local servicing rules before buying.

name: FS Series Cooling Fan
summary: Clip-on fans that blow across the water surface to cool the tank by evaporation. The range runs from the small FS-55 and single 120 mm FS-120 to the FS-600 bars with two to six fans in a row.
highlights: Mostly 12 V DC; FS-120 also in mains
Multi-fan bars (FS-602 to 606) for long tanks
bestFor: Cheap, low-power summer cooling for small and medium tanks that only run a couple of degrees too warm.
watchOut: Evaporative cooling means you will top up water more often, and fans only knock off a few degrees.

name: CJY Series Air Pump
summary: A rounded, modern-looking air pump range with a stepless electronic output control and an internal baffle to quieten the pulse. Seven sizes run from 1 to 15 L/min.
highlights: Internal labyrinth baffle for quieter running
bestFor: Anyone wanting adjustable aeration, from a nano sponge filter up to a multi-tank air line.

name: U Series Air Pump
summary: Tiny, low-power air pumps for nano tanks, sponge filters and air stones. The U-9900 is a twin-outlet version in the same small body.
highlights: 2 to 4 L/min, or 2 x 3.2 L/min on the U-9900
bestFor: Nano and small tanks running a sponge filter or a single air stone.
watchOut: Low pressure (0.009 to 0.012 MPa) limits it to shallow tanks and short air lines.

name: SC Series Air Pump
summary: An upright, compact air pump in single and twin outlet versions. Nothing fancy, just steady air for a sponge filter or two.
highlights: 3.2 L/min single or 2 x 3 L/min twin
Stands upright to save shelf space
bestFor: Small to medium tanks running one or two sponge filters or air stones.

name: S Series Air Pump
summary: An older, blue-shelled range with rubber diaphragms and no oiling needed. Single and twin outlet models, plus the S-4000B with four outlets and electronic control for multi-tank setups.
highlights: 4 to 4.2 L/min single, 2 x 4 L/min twin
S-4000B: four outlets at 3.2 L/min each
bestFor: Budget aeration for one tank, or the S-4000B for a small rack of breeder tanks.

name: SE Series Air Pump
summary: Small, quiet air pumps in four sizes, the larger two with twin outlets. A sensible cheap choice for a bedroom tank where noise matters.
highlights: Twin outlets on SE-314 and SE-315
bestFor: Nano to medium tanks where a quiet, low-power pump is the priority.

name: S-1800 AC/DC Air Pump
summary: A twin-outlet air pump that switches automatically to its internal rechargeable battery, or an external 6 V DC source, when the mains goes off. Keeps oxygen flowing through a power cut.
highlights: Automatic switch between mains, internal battery and external DC
bestFor: Keepers in areas with regular power outages who want aeration to carry on without them.
watchOut: Boyu does not state battery run time for this model.

name: S-1801 Lithium AC/DC Air Pump
summary: A slim twin-outlet air pump with a built-in lithium battery that takes over automatically if the mains fails. Comes in several bright colours.
bestFor: Load-shedding and power-cut backup for a single tank.
watchOut: Run time on battery is not published.

name: DR Digital Heater
summary: A newer glass heater with a small LED readout of the water temperature built into the tube, plus dry-run and overheat protection. Six sizes from 50 to 300 W.
bestFor: Everyday tropical tanks where you want to see the temperature without a separate thermometer.
watchOut: Glass heaters sit inside the tank, so plan a spot with good flow and hide it behind hardscape.

name: HT Adjustable Heater
summary: A basic adjustable glass heater with a dial on top and a printed thermometer strip on the tube. Six sizes from 50 to 300 W.
highlights: Printed temperature scale on the tube
bestFor: Budget heating for community and planted tanks.
watchOut: Dial-type heaters drift; check with a separate thermometer.

name: PTC Digital Heater
summary: A plastic-shelled PTC heater with an external controller, digital display and several probes. PTC elements heat quickly and run cooler on the surface than a glass element. High-wattage models for big tanks.
highlights: PTC element in an industrial plastic shell
bestFor: Large aquariums that need serious heating with accurate control.
watchOut: Overkill for most home planted tanks; the smallest model is 300 W.

name: TR Titanium Heater
summary: A thin titanium tube heater run from an external controller with an LED temperature readout. Titanium will not shatter, which is reassuring with large fish or in a sump.
bestFor: Sumps, large tanks or tanks with boisterous fish where a glass heater could crack.

name: GR Glass Heater
summary: A glass heater with a separate controller box showing the temperature on an LED display. Same concept as the titanium TR, in a cheaper glass tube.
bestFor: Medium tanks where you want an easy-to-read set point on the outside of the tank.

name: DR-9 Series Heater
summary: The older DR heater range, a glass tube with a built-in controller and LED display, plus dry-run and overheat protection. Seven sizes from 50 to 300 W.
bestFor: General tropical tanks on a budget.

name: Submersible UV Steriliser
summary: A UVC lamp in a quartz sleeve that sits inside the tank or sump rather than inline on a hose. Six sizes from 4 to 20 W.
highlights: Goes directly in the tank or sump
bestFor: Knocking out a green water bloom or running in a sump on a larger system.
watchOut: An open UV lamp in the display tank needs care, and it will not fix the nutrient imbalance behind an algae bloom.

name: CL Clamp Lamp
summary: Small clamp-on lamps with an adjustable aluminium head. The P models take PL compact fluorescent tubes, the L models use LEDs. Old-school but fine for a nano.
highlights: PL fluorescent (5 to 13 W) or LED (1.2 to 2.2 W)
bestFor: Nano and small tanks with low-light plants.
watchOut: The LED versions are very low wattage and will only grow the easiest plants.

name: ZN WiFi LED
summary: A slim aluminium LED bar with app control over timing, brightness and colour, including a 24-hour sunrise-to-sunset cycle. There is also an IR remote.
highlights: App control of timer, brightness and colour
bestFor: Planted tanks from 45 to 90 cm where you want scheduling and colour control on a budget.
watchOut: Boyu gives no PAR or lumen data, and lists the ZN-60 at the same length as the ZN-45, which looks like a sheet error.

name: CM-10 LED Clip Light
summary: A compact clip-on LED panel with touch control and several lighting modes. Runs on a low-voltage adaptor.
bestFor: Nano tanks and desktop scapes with easy plants.
watchOut: No spectrum or PAR data published.

name: CB Ultrathin LED
summary: A basic, very thin white LED bar with extendable brackets that rest on the tank rim. Five lengths from 50 to 140 cm.
bestFor: Low-tech planted and community tanks where you just need decent white light.
watchOut: No dimming, timer or published PAR, and wattage per length drops off on the longest bars.

name: ZN-800 / ZN-1600 Arm LED
summary: Fan-cooled LED spots on a gooseneck arm that clamps to the tank edge. The ZN-800 is a single puck, the ZN-1600 a twin-lens bar with app control. Knobs let you dim and shift the colour temperature.
bestFor: Open-top tanks where you want a hanging-style look without a ceiling mount.
watchOut: The colour dial runs between blue and white, which hints at a marine focus, and there is no PAR data.

name: Cornucopia Betta Cube (DY-150)
summary: A tiny betta cube with an LED in the lid, offered in several pastel colours. It is about 20 cm on each side, so very small.
bestFor: A single betta on a desk, with a few easy plants.
watchOut: Very small water volume means temperature and water quality swing quickly, and no filter is listed.

specs.Colours: Green, red, orange, black, white, yellow

name: Accord LED Desk Aquarium (BG-29)
summary: A novelty office aquarium that combines a small tank with a pen holder, digital calendar and gooseneck LED. It runs on low voltage and has an undergravel filter.
highlights: Pen holder and digital clock/calendar built in
bestFor: A desk ornament with a couple of easy plants or a few shrimp.
watchOut: The tank is only 12.8 cm tall and the pump and light are tiny, so treat it as a novelty.

specs.Voltage: AC 230/115 V (24 V to pump and light)

name: Refinement Aquarium (JDG-270)
summary: A small cube tank with a coloured frame, a swivelling lamp arm and built-in filtration. It ships with a 9 W energy-saving lamp, though Boyu says LED options exist.
bestFor: A beginner nano cube for easy plants.
watchOut: The standard 9 W compact fluorescent lamp is dated and will need replacing sooner than an LED.

name: Arts LED Aquarium (ME-175)
summary: A small framed desktop tank with a built-in filter and clip LED. Two slightly different heights, several frame colours.
bestFor: Office desks and first nano tanks with low-light plants.
watchOut: The 2 W LED is only enough for undemanding plants like mosses and Anubias.

name: Magic LED Aquarium (ME-213 / ME-270)
summary: A compact cube tank with a lid-mounted multi-mode LED and touch controls, running on 12 V. The ME-270H and 270RH are taller, with an external filter; the RH adds ultra-clear glass and an IR remote.
highlights: Feeding and ventilation holes in the lid
ME-270RH: ultra-clear glass and IR remote
bestFor: A tidy nano on a desk or shelf with easy plants.
watchOut: The lid covers the top fully, which limits emersed growth and plant choice.

name: Mia LED Aquarium (DSN-315)
summary: A small curved-lid desktop tank with a submersible filter and LED. About 32 cm long.
bestFor: A simple starter nano.
watchOut: The 0.6 W LED is a display light; plants beyond mosses and Anubias will struggle.

name: MS Series Aquarium
summary: A tidy lidded nano range with a top biological filter and a touch-controlled multi-mode LED. Three sizes from 20 to 45 litres.
bestFor: Beginners wanting a complete small tank for easy plants, shrimp or a betta.
watchOut: Low light output (5 to 7 W) suits low-light plants only.

name: DY Series Tabletop Tank
summary: Small tabletop tanks with the pump in the base, so water and electrics are kept apart, plus a multi-stage bottom filter and surface skimmer. Round and rectangular shapes, with or without A styling.
highlights: Motor sits in the base, separated from the water
Flow valve to cut water noise
bestFor: A betta or a few shrimp on a desk.
watchOut: Very small volume, so it needs regular small water changes.

name: MEZ Intelligent Aquarium
summary: A tall, lidded nano with a multi-mode LED whose brightness and colour you can adjust. The A versions use touch control; the standard versions add app control with a 24-hour natural light cycle. It runs an external filter.
highlights: Adjustable brightness and colour, app control on non-A models
bestFor: A compact planted or community tank with some lighting control built in.
watchOut: Tall, narrow tanks are harder to light well at the bottom and to aquascape.

name: Happy Family Aquarium
summary: A rounded all-in-one tank with filtration hidden in the hood and back. The fuller versions come loaded with a protein skimmer, UV, heater and night LED; the B versions keep it to pump, media and light, which is what a freshwater keeper needs.
highlights: A versions add heater, UV and protein skimmer
bestFor: Someone wanting a complete, ready-to-go medium tank without piecing together equipment.
watchOut: The skimmer on the A models is pointless in fresh water, and the HS-60 standard model uses a 150 W halogen lamp.

name: FY-10 Aquarium
summary: A clean, rimless-look glass tank with a lift-off lid carrying a detachable LED and an internal filter box. Designed to look good viewed from above as well as the front.
highlights: Detachable LED on a removable lid
bestFor: A starter planted or shrimp tank that looks neater than most kit tanks.
watchOut: Boyu does not publish volume, flow or light wattage.

name: FG Series Aquarium
summary: Simple glass tanks with a separate LED unit and an optional hang-on waterfall filter. Three sizes from 41 to 62 cm long.
bestFor: A basic glass tank for a budget planted or community setup.
watchOut: Filter is optional and specs beyond dimensions are not given.

name: HG Series Aquarium
summary: A glossy, colourful lidded tank with a top biological filter, digital clock, water temperature readout and a touch-controlled LED. Three sizes from 32 to 80 cm long, in seven colours.
bestFor: A bright, family-friendly tank with easy plants.
watchOut: Light output is low for the size, especially on the HG-800 (2 x 10 W).

specs.Colours: White, black, orange, green, yellow, red, pink

name: MT Mini Aquarium
summary: A curved-front kit tank with an internal biological filter, LED tubes and small cooling fans in the hood. Three sizes from 25 to 80 litres.
highlights: Internal bio filter with sponge, balls, carbon and ceramic
LED tubes plus 12 V hood fans
bestFor: Beginners after a complete kit for easy plants and small fish.
watchOut: The curved front distorts the view and makes aquascaping harder.

name: BYG Series Aquarium
summary: A cylinder-look tank with a split, flip-up lid made of two half-circles, a top biological filter and built-in lighting. Two sizes, 26 and 86 litres.
bestFor: A decorative round-style tank for easy plants and small fish.
watchOut: Curved glass is harder to scape and photograph, and light wattage is not clearly listed.

name: LJ Series Aquarium
summary: Hexagonal-fronted tanks with a flip-up ABS hood, top biological filter and tube lighting. Three sizes from 22 to 68 litres. Boyu lists these on its Chinese pages only.
bestFor: A compact display tank for a few fish and easy plants.
watchOut: The lighting is energy-saving tube based rather than modern LED.

name: ZJ Series Aquarium
summary: Curved-front lidded tanks with an internal pump feeding a top filter and a lid LED. Sizes from 20 to 84 litres; the A versions are taller.
highlights: Top filter fed by an internal pump
bestFor: Beginners after a complete medium kit tank.
watchOut: Lighting is weak for the size (6 to 10 W).

name: E Series Cabinet Aquarium (EAF / EAZ / EAM / EDM / EHM / ELM)
summary: An open-top-look cabinet aquarium with a partitioned sump-style filter in the base, LED tubes and a wireless touch-screen controller. Boyu sells the same tank under six series codes that differ only in cabinet and trim styling.
highlights: Feeding hatch that takes an auto feeder
Titanium-gold trim (EAF, EAZ) or wood-finish cabinets (EAM, EDM, EHM, ELM)
bestFor: Large community or planted displays where you want filtration and lighting built into the furniture.
watchOut: The included LED tubes (2 x 15 to 2 x 20 W) are well short of what a demanding planted tank needs.

specs.Series codes: EAF, EAZ, EAM, EDM, EHM, ELM (P and D suffixes on some)

name: XF Suspension Aquarium
summary: An 80 cm tank on a matching cabinet with a multi-stage bottom filter, surface skimmer and a flow valve to keep the water noise down. The JE version is taller.
highlights: Multi-stage bottom filter with surface skimmer
bestFor: A medium planted or community display with everything included.
watchOut: The 18 W light is only enough for low to medium light plants.

name: LZ Modern Aquarium
summary: A large curved-front tank on a cabinet with a top filter and LED lighting in the hood. The single piece of bent front glass gives an uninterrupted view. A big range from 84 cm to 3 m.
highlights: Bent front glass, no corner seams
bestFor: Large community displays where a seamless front matters more than aquascaping flexibility.
watchOut: Every size uses the same 1,200 L/h pump, which is weak on the bigger tanks, and the hood limits lighting upgrades.

specs.Colours: Snowy white, birch, cherry, mahogany, black

name: LH Overlord Aquarium
summary: A deeper take on the LZ, with bent front glass, a top filter and hood LEDs, on a matching cabinet. From 85 cm up to 2.8 m.
highlights: Deeper tanks than the LZ (50 to 67 cm front to back)
bestFor: Big community or cichlid displays that suit extra depth.
watchOut: A single 1,200 L/h pump across the whole range is underpowered for the larger tanks.

specs.Colours: Snowy white, birch, cherry, mahogany, black

name: ZDT Classic Aquarium
summary: A traditional curved-front aquarium and cabinet set with lighting in the hood and a choice of filter systems. Boyu pitches the red and blue LED mix as plant and colour friendly. Sizes from about 80 cm to 1.5 m.
highlights: Red and blue enhanced LED lighting, some models add an 11 W PL tube
Several filter options in the range
bestFor: A classic furniture-style community tank for the living room.
watchOut: Hood lighting is modest and hard to upgrade; the A4 and B4 variants come without a listed pump.

specs.Colours: Birch, black, snowy white, cherry, mahogany
specs.Variants: A4 / B4 versions have 4 LED tubes and no listed pump

name: LE Yahuan Aquarium
summary: A tall, dark arowana-style display tank on a cabinet with a filtration system in the base, touch panel and remote. Seven sizes, including wider L versions.
bestFor: Big fish displays, or a large planted tank if you replace the lighting.
watchOut: Boyu does not publish dimensions or specs for this series, so check with a dealer.

name: LA Yayue Aquarium
summary: An aluminium-framed tank and cabinet aimed at arowana keepers, with cabinet filtration, a touch panel and remote. Narrow at 36 cm front to back.
highlights: Aluminium frame in silver, champagne gold or black
bestFor: Tall display tanks for large fish in a narrow space.
watchOut: Only 36 cm deep, which limits aquascaping depth, and the lighting is modest.

name: LK Series Aquarium
summary: A slim black or white tank and cabinet with filtration in the base. The A versions get a stronger pump.
bestFor: A medium display for a hallway or narrow room.
watchOut: Only 32 cm deep, and a single 10 to 16 W LED is weak for plants.

name: LB Yapin Aquarium
summary: Boyu's bigger arowana-style tank and cabinet, with stronger cabinet filtration than the LA and LK and three LED tubes. Standard 48 cm deep or wider 60 cm L versions.
bestFor: Large fish displays or a big community tank.
watchOut: Lighting is modest for a planted setup of this size, and the maker's table labels the widest model inconsistently.
